OUTDOOR 5: Learn basic skills for winter camping and travel including thermoregulation, avalanche awareness, proper winter weather clothing and equipment, common cold weather medical issues, and LNT for camping and travel. Field experience includes practicing travel techniques, snow shelter construction, snow slope evaluation, use of avalanche beacons, and winter route finding
OUTDOOR 10: This course is an introductory course. Students will learn skills necessary to get started exploring the world of indoor climbing. These skills include technical safety skills for bouldering and top-roped climbing, essential physical and mental skills, and strategies for training. Students will be taught with industry standard best practices in regards to safety, and provided with a multi-disciplinary approach to overall health and wellness. No experience necessary.
OUTDOOR 11: In this course students will have the opportunity to build upon basic principles associated with rock climbing. Student will further explore variations in climbing efficiency techniques, crack climbing techniques, and training methodologies to enhance their climbing experience and help prevent injuries. Students will be taught with industry standard best practices in regards to safety, and provided with a multi-disciplinary approach to overall health and wellness.Prerequisites: Rock Climbing 1 or at least 3 months previous climbing experience, current top-rope belay certification at the Stanford Climbing Wall
OUTDOOR 12: Learn technical and safety skills pertaining to sport lead climibing. Apply specific physical and mental training principals to assist improving lead climbing performance and preventing over use injuries.
OUTDOOR 14: Learn how to transition from indoor climbing facilities to outdoor rock climbing venues. Emphasis will be placed on evaluating risk, along with constructing and assessing safe anchoring systems using natural and bolted anchors.
OUTDOOR 15: Explore climbing safety systems as they apply to anchor building, self-rescue, impact forces, and belaying. Emphasis will be placed on constructing and evaluating safe traditional anchor systems as well as learning techniques for self-rescue in the single pitch outdoor rock climbing environment.
OUTDOOR 16: This course is an intermediate to advanced-level skill class that introduces students to the skills and techniques needed to climb multipitch sport routes. The class covers topics such as belaying from above, rope management and leader transitions, climbing in parties of three, basic rescue skills, and rappelling multiple pitches. This class will increase students' knowledge of gear and safety while climbing, and equip them with skills to pick appropriate multipitch routes for themselves..
OUTDOOR 30: Learn the fundamental skills and safety pracices for coastal sea kayaking. Topics include essential gear, strokes and maneuvering, rescues and recoveries, and understanding tides and currents. This course will consist of several trips to Half Moon Bay and other near by coastal kayak areas. Active participation is required. Course culminates in a student-planned trip to a local kayaking destination.
OUTDOOR 31: Sea Kayaking 2 is designed to introduce students with beginner to intermediate level kayaking skills to kayak touring. Sea Kayaking 2 will review and expand skills learned in Sea Kayaking 1, including basic strokes and maneuvering, rescues, and navigation. Sea Kayaking 2 will equip students with more advanced strokes and recovery methods, as well as introduce students to concepts relevant to planning sea kayaking expeditions. The class will include a multi-day kayaking trip to a local area.
OUTDOOR 43: This course is for the intermediate to advanced climber looking to increase their climbing fitness. Students will be exposed to both general and climbing specific training principles to help improve climbing fitness and prevent common overuse injuries. Students will be taught with industry standard best practices with regards to safety and provided with a multi-disciplinary approach to overall health and wellness.
OUTDOOR 50: The Rock Climbing : Rescue Skills class will equip students with the skills and understanding of principles to perform rescues in a multi-pitch setting. The class will cover rescue techniques from both a bottom-managed and top-managed site. The class will also cover hauling systems, how to set up releasable load systems, and rappelling with an injured climber. A strong emphasis will be placed on planning and preparedness, accident mitigation, and how to be ready in case of an emergency. The class will not include any training on medical skills. Students entering this class must have a strong foundation in climbing, including knowledge of anchors, belaying from above, rappelling, and some multi-pitch climbing experience.
OUTDOOR 80: This course will expose students to beginner mountain biking skills. Topics covered in this course include balance and body position, shifting, braking, climbing and descending, cornering, navigating obstacles, trail-side repair, basic maintenance, trail etiquette, and safety. Upon completion of this class, students will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to pick local trails and undertake personal mountain biking outings.
OUTDOOR 101: This course involves fundamental instruction in hiking skills and techniques. Students will engage in a variety of hikes that will help improve their overall physical, mental, and emotional well-being. Students will learn the conditioning associated with hiking, the selection of equipment, navigation, the Leave No Trace Principles, and basic first and survival topics, along with trip planning. This course will also utilize class instruction, assignments, and student participation to enable students to (1) understand the basic components of fitness, health, and wellness. (2) develop physical fitness and motor skills, and (3) gain knowledge to make intelligent choices that contribute to a healthy, active lifestyle.
OUTDOOR 103: Explore topics about adventure activity risk assessment, leadership style and values, industry standards, and wilderness equity and inlcusion through class activites, discussions, and reflections. Develop essential skills for individual and group sustainability in a backcountry setting including shelter in outdoor environments, equipment selection and use, travel techniques, water and nutrition needs, planning and preparation, and risk management. Course includes the participation in a weekend backcountry experience.
OUTDOOR 105: Introduction to essential skills for individual and group sustainability in a backcountry setting including shelter in outdoor environments, equipment selection and use, travel techniques, water and nutrition needs, planning and preparation, and risk management. Course requires participation in a weekend backpacking experience.
OUTDOOR 106: Students will gain experience with both the technical campcraft, leadership, and risk management, skills necessary for to lead adventure based outdoor experiences. These skills will then be put into practice during an intensive field-based experience at the end of the course. During this field-based experiences, students will engage with critical self-assessment process to better understand their own levels of competence.
OUTDOOR 119: Students will gain experience with site management, instructional practices, risk management through a combination of teaching and leading weekend adventure based experiences, discussion of industry trends in managing risks, and through immersive field experiences. Prerequisites: OUTDOOR 106
OUTDOOR 195: Provides students with the opportunity to instruct adventure based leadership or technical skills in a field setting under supervision. emphasis will be placed on lesson planning, content delivery, and assessment of student learning . Requires defined student goals/benchmarks prior to field instruction. Pre-requisite: OUTDOOR 106 and/or instructor approval.
OUTDOOR 199: Exploration of a topic (to be determined) not covered by the standard curriculum but of interest to faculty and students in a particular quarter. May be repeated with change of content. For more information regarding specific course titles and topics, please refer to the notes of each course section.
